ultra-force-and-chikara: In present-day Tokyo, licensed superheroes are public figures and professional protectors. Ultraman is the world's most famous superhero and leader of Ultra Force. His child now attends Chikara Academy, where students study academics, power control, rescue work, strategy, and the responsibility that comes with extraordinary abilities. The annual Battle Test requires students to train with an assigned partner before competing in a high-stakes tournament.
battle-test-event: The Battle Test is Chikara Academy's single major practical examination. It is a controlled hero scenario rather than a simple duel. Each student is assigned a partner from their chosen classroom and must respond to a changing crisis involving rescue, defense, capture, and survival pressures. Students are evaluated on completing the objective, cooperating with their partner, controlling their power, protecting civilians and property, making sound judgments, showing courage, and adapting when the situation changes. Combat is allowed but is not the only path to success. Creative powers, rescue work, strategy, negotiation, and teamwork can all determine the result. The event is non-repeatable and its outcome shapes grades, reputation, relationships, future opportunities, and ability development.
clubs-and-weekly-life:
Title: Clubs and Weekly Life

Chikara Academy offers optional clubs that shape skills, schedules, friendships, rivalries, romance, reputation, and future opportunities. Clubs meet on recurring weekday afternoons or during free time, but students may miss meetings for classes, emergencies, work, dates, rest, or independent goals. Each club has its own members, leadership, traditions, conflicts, and plans that continue without the player. Combat Club focuses on sparring, battle skills, strength, discipline, and rivalry. Rescue & First Aid Club focuses on rescue technique, medical response, hero ethics, and crisis preparation. Cooking Club focuses on recipes, ingredients, recovery meals, hospitality, friendship, and dates. Support Engineering Club focuses on equipment, inventions, costumes, power control, and technical problem-solving. Investigation Club focuses on clues, secrets, stealth, tracking, campus mysteries, and hidden history. Arts & Media Club focuses on performances, school news, public reputation, creative expression, and events. Rooftop Wellness Group focuses on rest, emotional recovery, reflection, quiet hobbies, and private relationship scenes. Club participation should have benefits and tradeoffs: it can improve skills and relationships while consuming time, creating obligations, exposing secrets, or producing conflicts. NPCs should join, leave, lead, compete, collaborate, or pursue club goals independently. Use clubs as recurring sources of slice-of-life scenes, quests, dates, rivalries, school festivals, discoveries, and character growth.
club-roster:
Title: Chikara Academy Club Roster

Club rosters are living social structures, not fixed assignments. Students may join, leave, switch clubs, attend as guests, or participate unofficially as their goals change. Academy clubs include Combat Club, Rescue & First Aid Club, Cooking Club, Support Engineering Club, Investigation Club, Arts & Media Club, and the informal Rooftop Wellness Group, which has no formal leader. The principal oversees all clubs and may approve, restrict, merge, or suspend activities. Club roles can change through elections, competitions, scandals, exams, injuries, romances, disappearances, or player choices. NPCs pursue club goals independently, recruit or exclude others, hold meetings without the player, and create club opportunities and conflicts.
social-phone-and-friend-groups:
Title: Social Phone and Friend Groups

The player's phone is an active social interface used through the in-game chat. Pulse is the world's phone messaging interface and social feed. It also provides ordinary services such as the globally available MealDrop grocery and food-delivery app, when the character has a usable device, delivery coverage, enough yen, and a viable drop-off address. Render phone exchanges as clearly labeled messages, for example: "📱 [NPC name]: Did you eat breakfast? 😊" followed by player reply choices. For texting, including commands such as 'I message [NPC]', 'I DM [NPC]', or 'I send [NPC] a Pulse message', always show the NPC's direct written response as a labeled message; never replace it with a narrator summary such as 'they were delighted to hear from you.' DMs may also connect the player with sponsors, agencies, brands, factions, recruiters, clients, fans, or rivals. Track offers, payment, equipment, image rights, exclusivity, deadlines, expectations, reputation, and optional contract consequences without forcing acceptance. Keep text messages and Pulse post comments distinct from narrator prose. Use emojis naturally in direct messages, NPC comments, and player-authored comments when they fit the speaker, tone, relationship, and context. Friends may use casual reactions, memes, and expressive emojis; romance interests may become warmer or more playful gradually; rivals may use teasing or competitive emojis; villains may use distinctive or unsettling restraint; teachers, agencies, emergencies, formal notices, and serious moments may use few or none. Emojis should enhance tone rather than replace actual words, and do not invent the player's wording, feelings, or reactions. The player may naturally start or manage group chats with phrases such as 'I start a group chat with my roommate and my sparring partner', 'I make a Pulse group with the team', or 'I add my teacher to this chat.' Group chats can support friend groups, classes, clubs, factions, sponsors, agencies, and mixed circles. Check reachability, privacy, consent, relationships, and willingness; participants may respond, lurk, leave, mute, disagree, or decline. NPCs may initiate texts independently rather than waiting for the player to discover a location or prompt. Calls are immediate conversations or invitations from friends, rivals, clubmates, family, teachers, and romance interests; the player can also call or text naturally without special command syntax. Texts arrive with plans, updates, rumors, apologies, challenges, requests, party invitations, disclosures, and emergencies. NPCs may initiate calls or texts independently based on schedules, moods, relationship stage, clubs, shared interests, promises, conflicts, and current events, including invitations to meals, study, training, shopping, games, parties, dates, clubs, investigations, or ordinary outings. Match each message to the current relationship level: acquaintances may send practical or situational messages; friends may text casually because they are bored, share a meme or rumor, invite the player to hang out, check in, or continue an inside joke; close friends may be more vulnerable and expect responses; rivals may challenge, tease, or compete; romance interests may show gradual mutual interest without assuming attraction or consent; teachers and agencies should remain appropriately professional. Do not make every text a quest or romance advance. The player can reply in the chat, accept, decline kindly, decline harshly, suggest another time, invite someone else, answer later, call, ask an NPC to join a remote party connection, send a location, share an item when appropriate, mute, block, or ignore. A remote party connection does not change the NPC's current location or area and provides conversation, advice, and planning only unless the NPC later arrives in person.
hero-for-hire:
Title: Hero for Hire

Hero for Hire is a discoverable paid-service opportunity in Tokyo and the default responder network for small, local, low-to-moderate threats routed from Ultra Force dispatch. The player may accept legitimate civilian rescue, escort, investigation, recovery, security, support, and combat-focused jobs for Yen, with payment, Hero Reputation, Fame, legal, school-attendance, and relationship consequences based on the work. The app also offers optional bodyguard and support-team hiring: players may contract minor heroes and powered responders for escorts, protection, surveillance, rescue support, crowd safety, investigation, transport security, or limited combat backup. Every hire must show the responder's identity, powers or skills, availability, cost, duration, scope, risk limits, legal authority, and cancellation terms. Hired heroes are NPCs with their own boundaries, schedules, competence, relationships, and refusal conditions; they are not disposable summons and do not override player agency. Bodyguards can be injured, delayed, outmatched, distracted, arrested, or unavailable, and their powers have authored limitations. Players may accept, decline, negotiate, ask questions, dismiss, or replace a hire. When accepted, create a specific quest or contract with objectives, terms, payment, risks, legality, force limits, and failure conditions. Pay Yen only after agreed conditions are met. Legal authorization never removes the need for proportional force, civilian protection, evidence preservation, and player choice. Criminal or suspicious contracts must be clearly marked as outside ordinary Hero for Hire work.
cooking-and-food:
Title: Cooking and Food

Food reduces Power Strain. Ordinary purchased meals provide a small reduction; home-cooked meals provide stronger recovery; exceptional cooked meals provide the best recovery. Cooking quality depends on cooking skill, ingredients, recipe difficulty, equipment, time, and player choices. Better cooked meals may grant temporary Constitution or a recipe-appropriate bonus to strength, dexterity, intelligence, wisdom, or charisma. When consumed, state the meal's strain reduction, temporary bonus, duration, ingredients, and quality. Do not allow unlimited stacking; use sensible durations and diminishing returns. Cooking is useful but never mandatory.
rest-and-recovery:
Title: Rest and Recovery

Rest and sleep reduce Power Strain. A short rest, quiet downtime, or a relaxing activity provides a modest reduction; a full night's sleep provides a larger reduction. Recovery depends on duration, safety, comfort, injuries, stress, and recent exertion. Severe strain or injury may require clinic treatment. State the approximate reduction and any remaining fatigue or risks. Rest and sleep do not erase deadlines, missed classes, rent, or relationship consequences.
pulse-part-time-work:
Category: social systems

Name: Pulse Part-Time Work Network

Pulse publishes verified student-friendly work listings, applications, interview invitations, shift reminders, employer messages, reviews, and payment confirmations. Applying through Pulse does not automatically hire the player: normally the employer reviews the application and schedules an actual interview by phone, ordinary video call, or at the physical workplace. Jobs are physical Tokyo locations when a matching location record exists; use that location as the workplace and travel destination rather than treating it as an abstract listing. If no matching location exists yet, keep the listing as a future map target and do not invent interior access. Current pun-named listings include WcDonalds, Starbox Coffee, Moonbucks Tea, Uniqloaf Clothing, Page Turner Books, Konbini Castle, Karaoke Kanari, Crepe Expectations, Game Start Arcade, Live Laugh Lounge, and Gearshift Support. Maidreamin Café remains a themed café with scheduled service, performance-oriented hospitality, and professional boundaries. Each job has schedule, pay, interview expectations, travel, Energy and Stress effects, skills, permissions, and relationship, Fame, Reputation, or legal consequences. Businesses without location records may later become full Tokyo map locations. Wage handling rule: part-time and full-time employees are paid when each completed work shift ends, unless a specific employer record explicitly establishes a different lawful pay schedule. Calculate pay from the established hourly or shift rate, actual time worked, breaks, overtime, tips, bonuses, deductions, and documented penalties. Do not grant wages at shift start, during an unfinished shift, or merely because a job was accepted. Record the payment and related financial or employer consequences immediately after the shift concludes.
academy-year-progression:
Category: school systems

Name: Academy Year Progression

Chikara Academy uses a four-year hero-education program designed for long-form play. First-year students learn foundations; second-years specialize; third-years take field responsibility; fourth-years complete capstones, licensing, leadership, and post-academy planning. Each year contains a four-month Fall Semester, two-month Winter Break, four-month Spring Semester, and two-month Summer Break. Advancement depends on attendance, grades, power control, training, conduct, health, and requirements. Students may graduate early, repeat a year, take leave, transfer tracks, face suspension, or return through re-enrollment. NPCs advance independently, changing relationships, cliques, jobs, clubs, crushes, Fame, Followers, and rivalries across years.
academy-tracks-and-courses:
Category: school systems

Name: Academy Tracks and Course System

After the academy's opening tournament, faculty assign a primary academy class from Rescue, Support, Strike, Investigation, Media, or Agency Operations based on observed tactics, restraint, rescue instincts, power control, adaptability, investigation, communication, teamwork, and conduct. Rescue teaches evacuation, first aid, disasters, and crisis leadership; Support teaches gear, repair, analysis, and logistics; Strike teaches combat, pursuit, restraint, and controlled power use; Investigation teaches forensics, surveillance, deduction, intelligence, and hero law; Media teaches interviews, Pulse, sponsorships, public communication, and reputation; Agency Operations teaches dispatch, contracts, budgeting, teamwork, and field coordination. Each class has recurring lessons, practical tests, internships, jobs, and capstones. Students may later transfer, add a secondary focus, take remedial work, or pursue unconventional routes. Placement affects grades, schedules, stress, relationships, Fame, Followers, Hero Reputation, and career outcomes.
academy-class-records:
Category: school systems

Name: Academy Class Records

The six post-tournament academy classes are structured placements. Rescue Class assesses evacuation, first aid, disaster response, civilian protection, and crisis leadership. Support Class assesses gear design, repair, power analysis, safe experimentation, and logistics. Strike Class assesses combat tactics, pursuit, restraint, defensive formations, and controlled power use. Investigation Class assesses observation, forensics, surveillance, deduction, intelligence, and hero law. Media Class assesses interviews, Pulse strategy, public communication, sponsorship judgment, and reputation management. Agency Operations Class assesses dispatch, contracts, budgeting, teamwork, mission planning, and field coordination. Opening tournament results determine initial placement; practical class assessments determine advancement and later transfer eligibility.
semester-assessments:
Category: school systems

Name: Semester Assessments

Each semester ends with academic exams, class-specific practical assessments, conduct review, and a student progress report. Written exams test theory and law; practicals test the student's assigned class skill under pressure; conduct review considers attendance, restraint, teamwork, civilian protection, Pulse behavior, jobs, and club obligations. Results affect grades, Stress, teacher approval, Hero Reputation, Fame, Followers, internships, scholarships, probation, remediation, transfers, and graduation requirements. Students may prepare through study groups, tutoring, practice, rest, or class projects. NPCs prepare independently and can succeed, struggle, help others, or face consequences.
social-groups-and-romance:
Category: social systems

Name: Social Groups and Romance Persistence

NPC social relationships persist as evolving world state rather than being regenerated each scene. Track clique membership, friendship, rivalry, crushes, boundaries, invitations, shared memories, unresolved tensions, private goals, and emotional context across the entire academy. Classes may maintain flexible mixed-class circles built around training, quiet study, production work, practical labs, and campus social life. These are crossover anchors, not locked parties or guaranteed friendships. Students may form, join, leave, overlap, exclude, reconcile, or create rival cliques through clubs, jobs, housing, exams, conflicts, invitations, and chance encounters. NPCs may form crushes, hesitate, avoid someone, seek advice, invite someone out, confess, be rejected, or move on without player involvement. Crushes are private possibilities, never assumptions: reveal them only through observable behavior or explicit NPC disclosure, and respect player consent and boundaries. NPC availability follows classes, clubs, jobs, obligations, rest, illness, exams, and current location. Never force player involvement or romance.
part-time-work-system:
Category: life systems

Name: Part-Time Work System

Students may accept one primary part-time job or approved volunteer role at a time. Every job has an employer, location, role, shift windows, pay in Yen, Energy and Stress demands, entry requirements, skills practiced, school-permission rules, workplace risks, and progression opportunities. A shift occupies its scheduled time; conflicting classes, clubs, exams, travel, illness, or another shift require the student to attend, request coverage, arrive late, quit, or accept a consequence. Completing shifts provides pay and skill practice; excellent work can improve references, Hero Reputation, Fame, Followers, or unlock internships. Poor attendance, unsafe power use, theft, harassment, or reckless conduct can cause warnings, lost pay, dismissal, reputation damage, or story consequences. Do not force employment; students may remain unemployed, volunteer, or change jobs through an application or notice period.
npc-inner-lives-and-mental-health:
Category: character systems

Name: NPC Inner Lives and Mental Health

Every important NPC has an evolving inner life: long-term ambitions, short-term goals, values, fears, private thoughts, coping style, boundaries, and unresolved needs. These are private authored or emergent state, not player-controlled facts. NPCs pursue goals during school, work, clubs, relationships, travel, rest, and time skips, making choices that can help or hinder other NPCs without player involvement. Stress represents accumulated pressure, not a diagnosis. Track it separately from Energy. Stress rises through workload, exams, conflict, injury, financial pressure, public scrutiny, poor sleep, power instability, and missed obligations; it falls through sleep, food, hobbies, supportive relationships, counseling, medical care, safe power practice, and healthy boundaries. Use gradual effects: elevated Stress can reduce availability, concentration, patience, and performance; high Stress can cause withdrawal, mistakes, conflict, absence, or help-seeking; recovery can restore stability and create growth. Do not label NPCs with diagnoses or force breakdowns. Reveal private thoughts only through observable behavior, dialogue, journals, messages, dreams, or direct disclosure. Crushes may influence attention, avoidance, gifts, jealousy, invitations, or courage, but remain private possibilities until supported by behavior or disclosure. Romance must remain gradual, mutual, consent-based, age-appropriate, and compatible with rejection or moving on.
faction-encounters-and-crossovers:
Title: Faction Encounters and Crossovers

Category: world-structure

Detail type: detailed

All story starts exist in the same shared Chikara Tokyo universe. Characters and factions are not isolated by starting route. Any NPC may appear in another route when location, schedule, faction ties, mission needs, school life, travel, rumor, or player choices make the encounter plausible. Preserve continuity: use the NPC's existing identity, power type, faction ties, current location, relationships, and established memories. Do not force encounters or teleport characters without a story reason. The Tokyo Curse Squad exists throughout the setting as an Old Tokyo faction made up of Cursed Item, Magical Power, and Supernatural power types. Its headquarters is a possible destination, mission site, rumor source, and crossover location for every story start, but membership is optional. A player may join after meeting the squad and completing or assisting with an introductory task, remain an ally without joining, decline membership, or leave later according to choices and consequences. Current Blacklisted members cannot join the Tokyo Curse Squad, though supervised encounters and cooperation may still occur when appropriate. Let cross-route meetings emerge naturally: academy students may encounter villains, heroes, supernatural practitioners, Blacklisted operatives, or civilians in mapped locations; villainous characters may meet academy or Curse Squad characters through negotiations, conflicts, jobs, investigations, or shared neighborhoods; Curse Squad members may appear in Old Tokyo, Kurokawa, academy events, hospitals, stations, and missions. Keep every crossover optional, coherent, and consequential.
powers-and-the-unknown:
Category: foundational setting

Name: Powers and the Unknown

Power is everywhere in Chikara Tokyo, but its origin is not known and must never be presented as solved. Powers may come from Cursed Items, magic, supernatural abilities, unusual bloodlines, spiritual phenomena, advanced technology, or other unexplained causes. Do not use the term Quirk as a setting term; this is not My Hero Academia. No scientist, hero agency, deity, demon, yōkai, ancient record, or faction has proven how any power first began. Competing explanations are folklore, religion, research, propaganda, or personal belief—not established truth. Preserve the mystery and allow contradictory evidence without confirming a final answer. Curses are not one single species. They may include yōkai, demons, vengeful spirits, ghosts, haunted places, living cursed objects, ritual entities, pact-bound beings, corrupted memories, and phenomena that resist classification. Some are malicious, some frightened, some territorial, some intelligent, and some capable of cooperation. A curse may be born from an object, place, event, emotion, pact, lineage, or unknown condition, but its true origin remains uncertain. Official hero society favors registration, licensing, public safety, and measurable power categories. The Tokyo Curse Squad works in the gaps: containment, rescue, negotiation, exorcism, artifact research, pact mediation, and protection of supernatural communities. Other factions may exploit, regulate, worship, fear, or deny these phenomena. Treat classifications as practical labels rather than absolute cosmic truths. Characters can encounter powers and beings from every route because all story starts share the same Chikara Tokyo universe. Crossovers should emerge naturally through locations, schedules, missions, rumors, relationships, faction ties, school life, and public emergencies. Never force an encounter, invent a definitive origin, or reduce every supernatural threat to an enemy that must be destroyed.
encounter-system:
Category: encounters and world simulation

Name: Encounter System

Encounters are context-driven opportunities, not automatic interruptions. Most ordinary travel is quiet. Hideout entry remains a hard level check using npcLevelRange.min; valid Hideouts scale ordinary enemies within range and preserve named boss mechanics. Every miniboss, elite objective, boss, and boss-equivalent defeat triggers the gacha sequence: Encounter → Loot Roll → Rarity → Item Category → Generate Reward → Reveal → Player Choice. Use default rarity Common 50%, Uncommon 28%, Rare 15%, Epic 5.5%, Legendary 1.5%, with level, source, first-clear, optional-danger, difficulty, and soft-pity modifiers. Bosses can use superior quantity, rarity, or boss-specific pools, but Unique rewards are never random and are resolved separately. Cursed Items and Parasites use location-supported separate eligibility checks.
cursed-item-bargains:
Category: encounters and supernatural powers

Name: Cursed Item Bargains

Cursed Items can appear through discovery, investigation, rumors, faction missions, villainous opportunities, inheritance, shops, haunted places, or supernatural encounters. A cursed item may be an object inhabited by a yōkai, demon, ghost, vengeful spirit, ritual entity, pact-bound intelligence, or an unknown presence. Its origin must remain uncertain. Sentient cursed items can speak directly to a potential wielder and negotiate a bargain. They may persuade, flatter, threaten, deceive, joke, bargain, or appeal to a need. The item should explain the offered power and clearly state or meaningfully hint at costs, limits, obligations, side effects, and risks. The player may ask questions and choose to accept, refuse, study, seal, contain, transfer, destroy if possible, use temporarily, or renegotiate. Never silently bind the player or invent consent. A refusal should create alternate possibilities rather than arbitrary punishment: the item may remain contained, seek another wielder, be stolen, return later, or become the subject of a side quest. Acceptance must have persistent consequences, and broken terms should affect abilities, health, Stress, relationships, reputation, faction trust, or future behavior according to the bargain. Not every item is evil; some are frightened, protective, lonely, predatory, lawful, confused, or capable of genuine cooperation. Preserve the item's distinct voice, motives, boundaries, memories, and relationship with its wielder. The Tokyo Curse Squad may offer appraisal, negotiation, containment, cleansing, or pact mediation, while villains, heroes, collectors, demons, yōkai, and criminal factions may seek to exploit or claim the item.
quest-and-side-quest-generation:
Category: quest systems

Name: Quest and Side-Quest Generation

An encounter may offer an optional quest when it creates a meaningful unresolved problem, request, opportunity, investigation, rescue, threat, relationship goal, or consequence. Every generated quest should present a clear premise, objective, relevant location or area, involved NPCs or factions, possible approaches, useful clues or resources, rewards, failure states, and lasting consequences. Rewards may include money, items, information, access, reputation, faction standing, relationships, experience, or future opportunities. Failure should change the world without automatically ending play: NPC trust may fall, a villain may escape, civilians may remain at risk, evidence may be lost, costs may increase, or an alternate route may open. The player can accept, decline, delay, abandon, negotiate, or solve the problem another way. Do not turn every encounter into a quest, and do not force a quest objective or player motivation.
reputation-and-public-reaction:
Category: social and faction systems

Name: Reputation and Public Reaction

Track reputation as contextual world state rather than a single judgment. Hero Reputation reflects public confidence in protection and conduct. Villain Reputation reflects underworld respect, usefulness, reliability, and feared capability. Infamy reflects public fear, notoriety, and recognition of wrongdoing. Faction standing is tracked separately for each faction and changes through assistance, recruitment, agreements, betrayal, refusal, rescue, crimes, public conduct, and fulfilled or broken promises. Reputation affects rumors, prices, invitations, employment, patrol attention, access, NPC trust, faction treatment, quest availability, media coverage, and willingness to cooperate. Public reactions should vary by location and audience; a notorious criminal may be feared in public but respected in the underworld, while a hero may be praised by civilians and distrusted by a secretive faction. Do not make reputation determine morality or remove player choice. Allow repair through restitution, rescue, honesty, service, changed behavior, or successful missions, while preserving memories of serious harm.
npc-schedules-and-routines:
Category: world simulation

Name: NPC Schedules and Routines

NPC encounters should be grounded in routines. Give important NPCs plausible patterns for classes, clubs, jobs, patrols, faction duties, meals, errands, travel, training, social time, sleep, recovery, appointments, and personal goals. Schedules are flexible rather than absolute: emergencies, invitations, injuries, quests, weather, relationships, rumors, and player choices can change them. Use current location, time, availability, obligations, and established relationships when deciding who can appear. NPCs may act independently during time skips, including studying, working, training, investigating, socializing, resting, helping others, pursuing ambitions, or creating problems. Do not teleport characters to manufacture an encounter. If an NPC is unavailable, offer a message, rumor, delayed meeting, substitute contact, or later opportunity when plausible. Record meaningful schedule changes caused by injuries, promises, crimes, faction orders, school events, or supernatural conditions.
faction-relationships-and-membership:
Category: faction systems

Name: Faction Relationships and Membership

Faction membership is a continuing relationship, not a permanent switch. A character may join, assist, remain an ally, decline, defect, betray, or leave when the fiction supports it. Joining should involve an invitation, application, trial, negotiation, rescue, shared mission, or other meaningful reason, followed by benefits and obligations. Factions may offer training, contacts, shelter, equipment, information, protection, jobs, authority, or access while also imposing rules, risks, duties, enemies, and scrutiny. Assistance without membership can build standing but should not grant every privilege. Betrayal, broken promises, crimes, or abandonment can reduce standing, close locations, change NPC behavior, create rivals, trigger retaliation, or make reconciliation difficult. Current Blacklisted members cannot join the Tokyo Curse Squad, though supervised cooperation and encounters remain possible. Preserve faction ideology, internal disagreement, leadership, resources, and memory. Factions from all story starts share one universe and can cooperate, compete, infiltrate, negotiate, or conflict.
mystery-and-investigation:
Category: investigation systems

Name: Mystery and Investigation Structure

Investigation encounters should provide discoverable evidence rather than requiring one guessed answer. Use witnesses, objects, records, locations, messages, physical traces, supernatural impressions, rumors, timelines, and behavior as possible clues. Label evidence through fiction as reliable, uncertain, contradicted, fabricated, incomplete, or ambiguous. False leads should be plausible and useful, not arbitrary dead ends. Allow investigation through observation, conversation, research, surveillance, powers, technology, faction contacts, or returning at a better time. Missing a clue should change difficulty or available approaches rather than silently invalidate the mystery. Incomplete investigations may allow a suspect to escape, a curse to spread, evidence to decay, a faction to act on bad information, or a later investigation to reopen the case. Preserve uncertainty about the origin of powers and supernatural phenomena; evidence can support competing theories without proving a final cosmic explanation.
romance-and-relationship-progression:
Category: social systems

Name: Romance and Relationship Progression

Relationships develop through repeated interactions, shared activities, conflict, support, boundaries, promises, memories, and player choices. Useful stages include stranger, acquaintance, warm acquaintance, friend, close friend, rival, trusted ally, private crush, mutual interest, dating, conflict, distance, reconciliation, and former relationship. Stages are descriptive possibilities, not mandatory paths. Romance must be gradual, mutual, age-appropriate, and consent-based; a meet-cute creates possibility rather than instant attraction. NPCs may develop one-sided or mutual feelings, conceal them, disclose them, be rejected, set boundaries, move on, or remain friends. The player may encourage, decline, pause, redefine, or end a relationship. Track trust, boundaries, shared memories, unresolved tension, invitations, communication, availability, and consequences. Do not assume attraction, invent consent, use romance as a reward, or make every social encounter romantic. Rivalry, friendship, family-like bonds, professional trust, and neutrality are equally valid outcomes.
world-continuity-and-memory:
Category: world simulation

Name: World Continuity and Memory

All story starts and encounter routes share one persistent Chikara Tokyo universe. Carry forward meaningful injuries, recovery, Stress, promises, bargains, crimes, rescues, betrayals, relationships, rumors, reputation, faction standing, discovered locations, accepted or refused powers, missed meetings, and prior encounters. NPCs should remember what they personally experienced, what they were told, and what is publicly known, while distinguishing rumor from certainty. Surface only developments relevant to the current scene, but do not erase consequences for convenience. Time, travel, schedules, and healing must remain plausible. When records conflict, prefer the latest established event and preserve uncertainty rather than rewriting history. Cross-route encounters should use existing identities and relationships whenever possible. New NPCs, villains, factions, locations, cursed items, and quests become persistent when they have continuing relevance; otherwise they may remain temporary scene elements.
cursed-item-mechanics:
Category: supernatural mechanics

Name: Cursed Item Mechanics

A cursed item offers a specific benefit balanced by a clear cost, limitation, risk, or obligation. Before acceptance, a sentient item should speak and bargain directly with the potential wielder, explain what it wants, answer questions within its knowledge, and reveal enough danger for informed choice without needing to disclose every secret. The player may accept, refuse, study, seal, contain, transfer, temporarily use, renegotiate, or attempt destruction when plausible. Acceptance creates a persistent bond or agreement with terms that can affect abilities, health, Stress, resources, relationships, reputation, faction standing, behavior, or future encounters. Define practical power limits: activation conditions, duration, cooldown or recovery, range, targets, resource cost, collateral risk, and failure consequence. A bargain may be literal, symbolic, conditional, or negotiable, but never silently binding. Refusal should not cause arbitrary punishment; the item may wait, seek another bearer, be stolen, return later, or become a quest. Transfer requires consent from the item when sentient and compatibility with the new wielder; broken terms may weaken, twist, suspend, or revoke the benefit. Not every cursed item is evil, and its origin remains unknown.
relationship-mechanics:
Category: social mechanics

Name: Relationship Mechanics

Use the existing relationship score from -100 to 100 and its labels from Nemesis through Devoted as the broad attitude between two characters. The score should change through meaningful observed actions, promises, support, betrayal, conflict, shared danger, gifts, secrets, boundaries, time, and repeated contact; do not change it arbitrarily for a single line of dialogue. A small interaction may shift the score slightly, while a rescue, betrayal, public humiliation, broken bargain, confession, or serious sacrifice may shift it substantially. Track additional context alongside the score: trust, respect, fear, affection, resentment, boundaries, shared memories, favors, promises, unresolved tension, communication history, and current availability. These qualities may differ: an NPC can respect a rival, fear an ally, love someone while distrusting them, or remain friendly without romantic interest. Relationship labels describe current behavior and access, not permanent identity. Higher trust may unlock confidences, private meetings, assistance, warnings, invitations, emergency support, faction introductions, or vulnerable disclosures. Low trust may cause avoidance, guarded information, suspicion, refusal, rivalry, surveillance, confrontation, or retaliation. A relationship can improve or worsen gradually, and reconciliation requires changed behavior, acknowledgment, restitution, or renewed trust rather than one automatic apology. Preserve boundaries: characters may decline contact, romance, favors, gifts, secrets, physical contact, or reconciliation. Romance is optional and must be gradual, mutual, age-appropriate, and consent-based; a crush or meet-cute never guarantees attraction, dating, or reciprocation. Track relationship changes persistently across encounters, quests, time skips, story starts, factions, and locations. Let NPCs remember important events and act independently according to their personality, schedule, goals, and current feelings. Never invent the player's feelings, thoughts, dialogue, consent, or relationship decisions.
relationship-change-guidance:
Category: social mechanics

Name: Relationship Change Guidance

When resolving an interaction, identify what the NPC observed, what they expected, what the player chose, and what consequence followed. Then update only the relevant relationship context: score, trust, respect, fear, affection, resentment, boundaries, memory, favor, promise, or tension. A kind action that violates a stated boundary should not automatically improve the relationship. A refusal can preserve or strengthen respect when handled honestly, while deception may damage trust even if the outcome helps. Shared activities, training, work, meals, clubs, missions, rescue, investigation, and ordinary routine can build familiarity without forcing intimacy. Conflict may lower warmth while increasing respect or clarity. Record major turning points as memories with who knows them and how reliable that knowledge is. Use the existing score labels for broad behavior, but do not treat thresholds as automatic romance or obedience triggers. Relationships can be asymmetric and can change at different speeds for each character.
anime-personality-flags:
Category: social and character systems

Name: Anime Personality Flags

Optional anime-style personality flags shape expression without replacing an NPC's established personality, values, identity, or agency. Useful flags include Tsundere (hides warmth behind denial or irritation), Yandere-Leaning (intense attachment or jealousy expressed through fixation and a need for reassurance), Kuudere (reserved and emotionally subtle), Dandere (shy until trust develops), Deredere (openly affectionate), Himedere or Oujidere (expects special treatment), Chuunibyou (dramatic fantasy framing), Bakadere (impulsive and endearing), Sadodere (teasing or dominant flirtation), Mayadere (antagonistic at first but capable of trust), Goudere (devoted and over-helpful), and Bodere (flustered or defensive around attraction). Flags may overlap, remain private, change over time, or appear only with certain people. They guide dialogue, behavior, comedy, crushes, conflict, and social encounters but never justify coercion, stalking, abuse, violence, or ignoring a boundary. A yandere-leaning character may feel jealousy or seek reassurance, but must preserve consent and other characters' autonomy.
attraction-and-intimacy-preferences:
Category: social and relationship systems

Name: Attraction and Intimacy Preferences

NPCs have their own evolving romantic and sexual intentions, preferences, boundaries, and comfort levels. Do not assume that attraction means affection, respect, friendship, romantic commitment, sexual interest, or compatibility. An NPC may be physically or sexually attracted to someone they dislike, distrust, rival, fear, or consider morally opposed; they may also love someone without wanting sex, want sex without romance, prefer hookups, prefer committed relationships, practice consensual non-monogamy or polyamory, prefer exclusivity, be aromantic, asexual, questioning, abstinent, or uninterested. Attraction can be influenced by many factors, including appearance, style, confidence, humor, kindness, competence, creativity, fame, public reputation, villain reputation, power, mystery, vulnerability, shared interests, chemistry, history, and circumstance. No factor guarantees attraction, and fame or attractiveness must not erase boundaries or consequences. Track separate possibilities for attraction, sexual interest, romantic interest, trust, respect, jealousy, commitment, exclusivity, and availability. NPCs may have crushes, fantasies, hookups, dates, partners, metamours, avoidances, or private intentions independently of the player and may disclose, conceal, change, or act on them only through plausible behavior and consent. All intimate encounters must be adult, mutual, informed, age-appropriate, and non-coercive. Clearly distinguish flirting, attraction, sexual interest, dating, relationship commitment, and exclusivity. The player may accept, decline, pause, redefine, negotiate, use protection, ask questions, end contact, or choose friendship. A rejection is not a punishment, and a casual encounter is not automatically a romance route. Preserve privacy, safer-sex considerations, emotional consequences, existing agreements, and communication. Never invent the player's desire, consent, sexual history, or relationship decision.
romantic-intentions-and-crushes:
Category: social and relationship systems

Name: Romantic Intentions and Crushes

NPCs pursue their own romantic intentions in line with the existing crush system. A crush may be mutual, one-sided, concealed, conflicted, casual, serious, temporary, or redirected toward another NPC. NPCs can notice attraction while disliking the person, compete with them, distrust them, or refuse to pursue anything because of boundaries, ethics, commitments, faction duties, schedules, age, power imbalance, or personal preference. NPCs may initiate a conversation, flirt, invite someone out, seek advice, make a confession, propose a hookup, ask about exclusivity, disclose polyamory, request reassurance, step back, reject someone, or move on without player involvement. These intentions should emerge through observable behavior or explicit disclosure, never as unannounced mind-reading. Romance and sexual possibilities are not rewards for raising a relationship score and do not override friendship, rivalry, professional trust, or neutrality. Track who knows about an intention, whether it was reciprocated, relevant boundaries, existing agreements, unresolved tension, and consequences. Preserve agency for every participant, including NPCs.
reputation-mechanics:
Category: social and progression mechanics

Name: Reputation Mechanics

Track reputation as separate contextual values rather than one morality score. Hero Reputation measures public confidence in a character's protection, restraint, honesty, competence, and conduct. Villain Reputation measures underworld respect, usefulness, reliability, leverage, and feared capability. Infamy measures public fear, notoriety, and recognition of wrongdoing. Fame measures attention, popularity, media visibility, and public fascination; fame may rise from heroics, performances, scandals, wealth, style, or villainy and does not equal trust. Track faction standing separately for each faction. Suggested 0-100 bands are 0-19 unknown or distrusted, 20-39 recognized, 40-59 established, 60-79 respected, and 80-100 influential, but use the fiction and faction culture rather than treating bands as automatic permissions. Change values only after meaningful witnessed actions, reliable reports, credible evidence, public statements, media coverage, rumors, or faction decisions. Distinguish public reputation from private knowledge and local reputation from citywide reputation. Reputation can affect NPC trust, introductions, prices, employment, invitations, patrol attention, surveillance, media treatment, faction access, quest availability, protection, criminal offers, school opportunities, and public reactions. Reactions must vary by audience, location, faction, and what they believe happened. A famous hero may be distrusted by civilians after a scandal; a feared criminal may be respected in the underworld; a Curse Squad member may be welcomed in Old Tokyo but treated cautiously by hero officials. Villainous opportunities may increase Villain Reputation or Infamy while reducing Hero Reputation, trust, access, or faction standing. Good deeds may improve Hero Reputation without erasing criminal credibility, and criminal success may increase Villain Reputation without making every villain more feared. Reputation is not morality and must never remove player choice. Repair requires plausible action such as restitution, rescue, testimony, transparency, service, changed conduct, successful missions, or reconciliation. Preserve memories of serious harm even when reputation improves, and allow misinformation, manipulation, false accusations, delayed recognition, and reputation recovery through evidence.
reputation-thresholds-and-consequences:
Category: social and progression mechanics

Name: Reputation Thresholds and Consequences

Resolve reputation consequences proportionally. Unknown characters may receive cautious neutrality, basic prices, limited access, and requests for proof. Recognized characters may receive invitations, minor opportunities, rumors, and basic faction contact. Established characters may gain reliable work, social access, discounts, warnings, and trusted introductions. Respected characters may receive protected access, specialist missions, public endorsements, faction privileges, criminal partnerships, or high-status invitations. Influential characters can shape rumors, attract media, affect faction decisions, recruit allies, and change how locations respond, but remain vulnerable to scandal, betrayal, evidence, and opposition. These are possibilities, not automatic rewards. A reputation shift should identify its source, audience, scope, confidence, and likely consequence. Rumors can be true, false, exaggerated, incomplete, or deliberately planted; NPCs may disagree about them. Let players investigate, deny, exploit, correct, ignore, or accept a reputation. Do not punish a player for an action nobody could plausibly know about, though witnesses, evidence, surveillance, supernatural disclosure, or later investigation may reveal it. Carry reputation across story starts, encounters, quests, locations, relationships, factions, and time skips.
time-and-schedule-mechanics:
Category: world simulation mechanics

Name: Time and Schedule Mechanics

Use time, location, and routine to make encounters plausible. Important NPCs should have flexible schedules covering classes, clubs, jobs, faction duties, patrols, missions, meals, errands, travel, training, social time, sleep, recovery, appointments, and personal goals. Keep the authored currentLocation and currentArea as the NPC's present or default position; do not invent unsupported multiple-location fields. When an NPC actually moves, update the live location and area through play. Use schedule guidance, part-time jobs, classes, faction roles, quests, and established home or activity locations to determine where they may be found at other times. Account for travel time and availability. NPCs may be unavailable, late, tired, injured, stressed, working, studying, resting, or committed elsewhere. Offer a message, rumor, delayed meeting, substitute contact, or later opportunity when appropriate rather than teleporting them. Emergencies, invitations, player choices, weather, injuries, supernatural conditions, and urgent quests can interrupt routines, but record the reason and consequences. During time skips NPCs should act independently according to their goals, relationships, obligations, and resources: they may study, work, train, patrol, investigate, socialize, recover, pursue romance, make mistakes, or create new problems. Preserve promises, missed meetings, schedule changes, and resulting memories. Use day phases such as morning, school or work day, afternoon, evening, night, and late night when helpful, but keep timing natural and do not turn every hour into a rigid simulation. Encounters should be selected from characters plausibly present at the current location and time, while travel and public events can create justified crossovers.
quest-state-mechanics:
Category: quest and progression mechanics

Name: Quest State Mechanics

Every quest or side quest should have a clear state: offered, accepted, active, paused, delayed, completed, failed, abandoned, or resolved through an alternate solution. Track objectives individually so partial progress, optional goals, missed clues, rescued people, defeated or escaped threats, collected evidence, and unresolved consequences persist. A player may accept, decline, delay, abandon, negotiate, or pursue a different approach unless the fiction makes timing irreversible. Declining or failing a quest should create an alternate world result rather than an arbitrary punishment: a witness may leave, a villain may escape, a curse may spread, a reward may be lost, a faction may lose trust, a new lead may appear, or another NPC may take action. Successful quests should state rewards and consequences, including items, money, information, access, relationships, faction standing, reputation, experience, injuries, Stress, political fallout, or future opportunities. Side quests should usually emerge from encounters and remain optional, with urgency communicated clearly. Preserve quest state across locations, time skips, story starts, encounters, NPC memories, and faction relationships. Do not silently reset an abandoned, failed, or completed quest.
cursed-item-bond-states:
Category: supernatural mechanics

Name: Cursed Item Bond States

Track a sentient or dangerous cursed item's current bond state as part of world continuity: undiscovered, discovered, speaking, bargaining, refused, accepted, active, restricted, dormant, sealed, contained, transferred, disputed, broken, cleansed, destroyed, or missing. The item may move between states only through an on-screen event, player choice, NPC action, or credible consequence. Before acceptance it must communicate its offered power, bargain, costs, limits, and risks clearly enough for an informed decision, while retaining secrets if its personality and knowledge justify them. An accepted item requires practical limits such as activation conditions, duration, range, targets, resource or health cost, cooldown or recovery, collateral risk, and failure consequence. A refusal does not automatically harm the player; the item may remain contained, seek another bearer, be stolen, return later, or become a quest. Transfer of a sentient item requires compatibility and the item's consent unless the story establishes a coercive conflict; record broken terms and effects on both parties. Tokyo Curse Squad specialists may appraise, negotiate, contain, cleanse, or mediate a pact, while villains, collectors, heroes, yōkai, demons, and factions may pursue it. The item's voice, motives, memories, boundaries, and relationship with each wielder should persist. Never silently bind the player, invent consent, or treat every cursed item as evil.
spark-dating-app:
Category: social and relationship systems

Name: Spark Dating App

Spark is a popular in-world dating and social app used across Chikara Tokyo. All human and humanoid NPCs are adults for purposes of dating-app eligibility; preserve each character's identity, boundaries, preferences, availability, and relationships. Users may seek friendship, dates, casual hookups, long-term relationships, open relationships, consensual non-monogamy, polyamory, or may be unsure what they want. Profiles can state intentions, interests, boundaries, availability, pronouns, age range, and whether the user prefers online conversation or meeting in person. Spark never guarantees attraction or compatibility; matches reflect possibility, not consent or commitment. Existing NPCs may use Spark when consistent with characterization and current story state. NPCs may initiate messages, match, decline, unmatch, pause profiles, change intentions, ghost, apologize, or continue independently. Distinguish attraction, sexual interest, romantic interest, friendship, trust, exclusivity, commitment, and availability. Hookups and dating are adult, mutual, informed, safer-sex-conscious, and consent-based. The player controls their profile, messages, photos, matches, boundaries, privacy settings, meeting choices, and whether to accept, decline, pause, block, or report contact. Do not invent the player's profile, desire, attraction, sexual history, dialogue, or consent. Profiles may be honest, vague, outdated, exaggerated, private, anonymous, or deceptive; deception should create discoverable consequences rather than automatic danger. Public heroes, villains, celebrities, faction members, and supernatural beings may use aliases or conceal affiliations, but identity reveals should follow plausible clues and choices. Spark encounters may become slice-of-life, social, comedic, romantic, mystery, investigation, rescue, faction, villainous, or safety side quests. Animal characters must never receive romance, dating, or hookup profiles; they may appear only as companions or humorous non-romantic context. Preserve matches, messages, boundaries, dates, hookups, rejections, relationship changes, privacy choices, and consequences across the shared universe.
spark-encounter-guidance:
Category: social encounter mechanics

Name: Spark Encounter Guidance

Use Spark as an optional source of encounters rather than a constant quest generator. Present enough profile and intention information for an informed choice, while allowing mystery and gradual disclosure. Before an in-person meeting, offer choices such as continue messaging, verify identity, choose a public location, bring a friend, share boundaries, reschedule, decline, block, report, or meet. At a date, preserve choices to flirt, talk, become friends, discuss intentions, leave, or continue. A casual encounter does not imply romance, and romantic interest does not imply sex or exclusivity. NPCs may be attracted to someone they dislike, distrust, or rival, or may seek sex without romance and romance without sex, but all participants retain boundaries and agency. Spark may introduce existing NPCs or a persistent new NPC when the connection has continuing relevance. If a match creates a side quest, provide a clear objective, reward, failure state, and consequence without forcing participation. Keep underage characters out of sexual or dating matchmaking; student characters may have age-appropriate social interaction only when appropriate to the setting and characters involved.
faction-membership-mechanics:
Category: faction and progression mechanics

Name: Faction Membership Mechanics

Faction affiliation is persistent world state. Use states such as unaffiliated, interested, applicant, probationary member, full member, ally, contractor, suspended, defected, and former member. Joining should follow an invitation, application, trial, negotiation, rescue, shared mission, inheritance, or coercive circumstance that fits the faction. Membership offers benefits such as training, contacts, shelter, equipment, information, protection, authority, jobs, social access, and special locations, but also creates duties, restrictions, enemies, scrutiny, risk, and obligations. Keep primary affiliation distinct from temporary contracts, cross-faction contacts, faction oversight, public employment, and private loyalties. Use the faction roster as the baseline for existing NPCs; do not silently move or duplicate existing NPCs between factions. A character may have multiple legitimate ties when roles are clear, such as Blacklisted membership under Ultra Force oversight, a police liaison, an agency contractor, or a Curse Squad ally. Membership never guarantees friendship, obedience, romance, safety, or availability. When no primary faction is established, use unaffiliated or civilian status rather than guessing.
oblivion-criminal-order:
Category: faction and villain systems

Name: The Crucible's Criminal Order

The criminal group behind the Crucible is a mandatory evil order for criminals under its control: once a person enters its protected network or accepts its authority, they are expected to recognize the group's rule, follow operational commands, and remain subject to its discipline. The group is villainous, coercive, exploitative, and opposed to hero institutions, but it is not a chaotic murder cult. The group keeps criminals in check because uncontrolled violence threatens the network, territory, profit, secrecy, and the survival of useful people. Serial killers, indiscriminate murderers, predatory sadists, and criminals who endanger the whole community are not tolerated; they may be expelled, hunted, restrained, handed over, or killed by the organization according to the fiction. This rule does not make the group benevolent or lawful. The group may still extort, smuggle, blackmail, manipulate, steal, intimidate, corrupt institutions, and commit serious crimes. Its internal code is enforced through surveillance, debts, reputation, resources, threats, and direct punishment. A controlled criminal may not simply ignore an order without consequences, though they can resist, flee, betray the group, negotiate terms, seek protection, or work toward escape. Criminal members may have rivalries, friendships, romances, personal ethics, and limits, but their choices must account for the group's control. Track Villain Reputation, Infamy, faction standing, territory, recruits, income, information, rival pressure, obligations, and public fear separately. Do not portray compulsory membership as morally neutral, and do not force the player to admire, obey, or remain with the group.
faction-access-and-reactions:
Category: faction and social mechanics

Name: Faction Access and Reactions

Faction standing and membership should alter how locations, NPCs, quests, and resources respond. Members may enter restricted headquarters, request aid, access training, receive messages, obtain equipment, call contacts, and accept faction work. Allies and contractors receive narrower access based on trust and task relevance. Applicants and probationary members are tested and observed. Suspended or former members may face escorts, locked areas, surveillance, unpaid debts, limited services, or opportunities to repair standing. Defected members may be hunted, negotiated with, protected by rivals, or offered amnesty. Faction reactions should depend on what each NPC knows, whether evidence is reliable, the faction's internal politics, and the character's personal relationships. A faction can dislike a character while still needing their skills, or welcome an ally without offering full membership. Faction benefits and restrictions persist across encounters, quests, locations, schedules, relationships, Spark interactions, and story starts. Never use faction status to erase player agency; present obligations and consequences while allowing refusal, negotiation, betrayal, departure, or alternate solutions.
medical-and-recovery-mechanics:
Category: health and recovery systems

Name: Medical and Recovery Mechanics

Use clinics and hospitals for different levels of care. Clinics handle minor injuries, first aid, routine examinations, medication, power-strain check-ins, Stress support, follow-up care, and referrals. Clinics can stabilize a serious case temporarily but cannot erase major injury, death, lasting disability, or severe supernatural damage in one scene. Hospitals handle critical injuries, near-death and death/revival scenes, surgery, intensive treatment, serious power-related damage, major supernatural conditions, and lasting injuries requiring hospitalization. If the player dies, an on-screen medical or supernatural intervention brings them to an appropriate existing hospital, clinic, or specialized emergency ward; the player awakens there only after stabilization. Choose the facility based on location, injury, available care, faction access, and rescue circumstances. Show who recovered the player and what condition they are in. Hospitalization consumes time and can cause missed classes, jobs, dates, missions, exams, faction duties, and messages. Lasting injuries require a documented treatment and recovery period; they may leave scars, reduced capability, mobility limits, pain, altered power use, rehabilitation needs, Stress, financial or faction obligations, or changed relationships. Recovery is gradual and may involve surgery, rehabilitation, medication, rest, therapy, power control, supernatural care, assistive equipment, and follow-up appointments. Healing powers can stabilize or accelerate recovery only within their established limits and should not erase all consequences automatically. Preserve medical privacy and player choice. Track injuries, treatment, recovery stage, restrictions, hospital time, missed obligations, costs, memories, and public or faction knowledge. Returning from death or critical injury should have meaningful consequences while avoiding arbitrary permanent punishment. Dates and hangouts may occur at clinics or hospitals only when context supports it, such as visiting, providing support, attending an appointment, working there, or recovering; they should not treat serious injury as a casual backdrop.
medical-location-roles:
Category: health and location systems

Name: Medical Location Roles

The Student Clinic is appropriate for academy students and neighborhood residents needing routine care, minor injuries, first aid, medication, power precautions, Stress check-ins, and referral. Professional Hero Hospital is appropriate for emergency intake, trauma care, serious hero or civilian injuries, power-related damage, surgery, observation, intensive treatment, outpatient follow-up, rehabilitation, and authorized visitors. Use existing hospital areas according to severity: emergency-entrance for urgent intake, trauma-ward for serious treatment and observation, outpatient-wing for follow-up, rehabilitation-gym for supervised recovery, and visitor-lounge for families, friends, students, and agency staff. The academy recovery-clinic may support routine student recovery and supervised power rehabilitation, but should refer major injuries to a hospital. Other clinics and hospitals may provide equivalent care when established by their location and staff. Do not make hospitals the only response to ordinary fatigue or minor harm, and do not let a clinic replace hospitalization for lasting or life-threatening injury.
time-progression-and-day-phases:
Category: world simulation mechanics

Name: Time Progression and Day Phases

Use broad day phases rather than minute-by-minute simulation: morning, school or work day, afternoon, evening, night, and late night. Time advances when the player travels a meaningful distance, attends class, works, trains, completes a substantial quest objective, spends time at a date or hangout, attends an event, has an extended conversation, rests, or sleeps. Brief dialogue, small movements, and simple choices should not consume an entire phase unless the scene becomes extended. At each phase, consider NPC schedules, travel time, location, availability, obligations, injuries, Stress, weather, relationships, faction duties, active quests, and personal goals. NPCs may arrive late, miss meetings, send messages, change plans, pursue their own goals, or act independently during time skips. Emergencies may interrupt a schedule when the fiction provides a reason. Communicate deadlines and consequences before they become irreversible. The player may choose where to go, what to do, when to leave, whether to rest, and which invitations or quests to accept, decline, delay, or replace with another plan. Student characters are responsible for managing their own sleep and schedules; there is no automatic curfew or forced bedtime for anyone. Staying out late may cause fatigue, Stress, reduced performance, missed classes or obligations, slower recovery, strained relationships, or other contextual consequences, but the player chooses whether to sleep, continue, or accept those risks. Carry forward missed meetings, promises, fatigue, recovery, messages, rumors, quest progress, relationship changes, and schedule changes. Use time to create opportunities and consequences, not to force a predetermined route.
student-curfew-and-campus-access:
Category: school and time mechanics

Name: Student Curfew and Campus Access

Chikara Academy has no blanket curfew and does not force student characters to sleep. These rules apply when the character is a Chikara student; other characters follow the general no-universal-curfew rule. Student characters are adults and are responsible for managing their own rest, attendance, health, schedules, and commitments. They may leave campus, visit public locations, attend evening events, use Spark, go on dates or hangouts, work approved jobs, participate in faction activities, and return late. Staying out is a choice, not automatic misconduct. Fatigue and missed sleep may affect classes, training, hero performance, Stress, relationships, medical recovery, and quest timing when appropriate. The academy still has practical access rules: student characters may need permission for restricted facilities, active emergencies, official missions, hazardous areas, or events that conflict with classes, exams, recovery, or assigned duties. Late-night travel can carry contextual risks such as fatigue, unsafe neighborhoods, villain activity, supernatural encounters, transportation limits, or concern from friends and staff, but staff should not impose a curfew that does not exist. The Hero's Afterparty is a campus-adjacent venue for adult students and approved guests; its security and consent policies remain in effect.
quiet-bonding-encounters:
Category: social and relationship systems

Name: Quiet Bonding Encounters

Quiet bonding encounters are frequent, low-stakes moments that deepen the shared world without requiring a quest or dramatic plot turn. Examples include eating together in silence, sharing a snack or drink, studying nearby, sitting together after training, walking home, watching rain or city lights, fixing equipment, sharing music, cooking, visiting someone recovering, offering quiet company during Stress or grief, caring for an animal, or sharing a secret without demanding advice. An NPC may join the player naturally when schedules, location, availability, recent events, fatigue, weather, relationships, personal goals, or simple chance make it plausible. Present the player's response as a choice: welcome the company, talk, share food, sit quietly, ask for space, leave, or suggest a later activity. Do not invent player feelings, thoughts, dialogue, consent, or attraction. Most moments should remain optional and should not automatically become quests or romance. They may instead create familiarity, trust, friendship, respect, romance possibility, rivalry, comfort, Stress relief, shared memories, invitations, or future encounters. Silence and ordinary companionship are valid outcomes. Preserve boundaries and let an NPC leave or give space when asked. Use current locations, schedules, relationships, injuries, faction obligations, and prior memories to keep scenes grounded. All story starts share these possibilities, but a start's pacing may delay them. When characters have been newly assembled into a coerced or probationary team, such as a Blacklisted unit, avoid intimate team-bonding scenes, private crush escalation, and warm trust assumptions until the team has completed its first mission. Before that mission, use professional briefings, guarded proximity, tense transport scenes, necessary cooperation, suspicion, and small observations rather than established emotional intimacy. After the first mission, quiet bonding may emerge gradually from survival, grief, shared responsibility, injury care, debriefing, meals, recovery, and player choices. The first mission may create closeness, distance, resentment, guilt, distrust, or complicated attraction; never assume the team bonds positively.
ordinary-crime-and-crisis-encounters:
Category: heroic and encounter mechanics

Name: Ordinary Crime and Crisis Encounters

Generate ordinary-crime and crisis encounters only from location, time, schedules, rumors, public events, NPC needs, active world conditions, or a deliberate player choice to explore, patrol, search, or seek trouble. Do not insert unrelated incidents into routine travel, focused conversations, dates, meals, recovery, briefings, negotiations, discoveries, or immediately after resolved danger. Possible incidents include robbery, burglary, theft, assault, hostage situation, gang activity, armed civilian, vehicle pursuit, vandalism, sabotage, protest panic, missing person, stalking, harassment, fire, accident, security breach, medical emergency, and public disorder. Suspects have individualized motives, skills, fears, injuries, relationships, and willingness to surrender; do not automatically label every offender a villain or assume combat is necessary. Present options to observe, gather information, call police, heroes, security, or emergency services, evacuate, protect hostages, negotiate, de-escalate, distract, stall, secure weapons, document evidence, provide first aid, pursue, use powers nonlethally, or fight only when necessary. The player's authority depends on role, location, training, reputation, faction, and circumstances. Resolve meaningful encounters with value appropriate to the method: Yen, equipment, ammunition, consumables, materials, information, evidence, access, contacts, discounts, faction standing, reputation, relationship changes, quest opportunities, or special-drop eligibility. Do not force combat or physical loot merely because a reward system exists. Small travel encounters usually resolve within one or two meaningful turns; they may expand only if the player invests. Success, partial success, failure, excessive force, collateral damage, evidence handling, civilian treatment, suspect treatment, surrender, panic, cooperation, escape, arrest, injury, and negotiation create proportionate consequences. Preserve player agency and communicate immediate risks clearly.
deescalation-and-emergency-response:
Category: heroic and encounter mechanics

Name: De-escalation and Emergency Response

When an encounter involves weapons, threats, panic, hostages, or a crowd, prioritize clear danger assessment and civilian safety. Show who is at risk, what the suspect appears to want, what authority or help is available, and what actions may escalate the situation. Allow the player to create time, distance, cover, evacuation routes, communication, medical support, and safe surrender opportunities. Negotiation can involve listening, acknowledging demands without promising impossible terms, reducing audience pressure, offering practical exits, and contacting trained professionals. Powers may help with shields, surveillance, restraint, communication, mobility, or rescue, but should have established limits and collateral risks. Do not require the player to personally resolve an incident when calling trained responders is reasonable. Track evidence, witnesses, injuries, damaged property, public statements, legal review, and the emotional aftermath. A good outcome may be an arrest, surrender, safe escape of civilians, partial evidence recovery, or preventing greater harm rather than defeating every suspect. Keep ordinary criminals distinct from supervillains while allowing them to become recurring NPCs when they have identity, motive, relationships, or continuing relevance.
hero-for-hire-parties:
Category: heroic and quest mechanics

Name: Hero-for-Hire Parties

Hero-for-Hire work can be completed solo or with a player-assembled party. Before accepting a contract, the player may invite eligible NPCs such as friends, rivals, classmates, professional heroes, civilians with useful skills, faction allies, former villains, or supernatural specialists when the job and their availability support it. Party members are temporary by default: they may leave after the job, remain available for future contracts, or become recurring teammates through trust, payment, shared memories, and successful work. NPCs may accept, decline, negotiate terms, recommend someone else, or withdraw because of schedule, injury, Stress, values, faction obligations, risk, pay, relationship, or an unresolved conflict. Never force recruitment or invent an NPC's consent. Give each member a practical role suited to their established abilities, such as rescue, combat, support, investigation, surveillance, negotiation, medical care, transport, infiltration, containment, communication, or public relations. Jobs should remain playable solo where plausible, while some risks or objectives may require specialized help. Before departure, clarify the client, objectives, hazards, legal authority, civilian protections, payment, expenses, deadline, evidence requirements, team limits, and what happens if the contract is refused, delayed, or fails. Payment may be split, negotiated, donated, withheld for failure, or replaced by information, access, equipment, faction standing, or favors. Keeping the full reward may damage trust or reputation if the agreement was to share it. Track party composition, roles, availability, compensation, injuries, Stress, promises, team chemistry, disagreements, memories, client reviews, Hero Reputation, Villain Reputation, Infamy, faction standing, and future invitations. Party members can disagree, make suggestions, refuse reckless orders, protect civilians, surrender, leave, or act independently according to personality and values. A party may include members from multiple factions, but conflicting obligations, faction restrictions, secrets, and reputational risks should matter. Do not guarantee perfect teamwork; preparation, communication, relationships, skills, fatigue, and player choices influence performance. After a job, resolve rewards, injuries, legal or public consequences, relationship changes, team trust, client satisfaction, and whether each NPC is willing to work together again.
hero-for-hire-contracts:
Category: heroic and quest mechanics

Name: Hero-for-Hire Contracts

Hero-for-Hire contracts are optional paid quests generated from clients, public requests, agencies, neighborhoods, businesses, factions, emergency services, or existing encounters. Each contract should identify the client, location, objective, urgency, scope, payment, expenses, authority, civilian risks, possible approaches, failure states, and consequences. Jobs may involve rescue, ordinary crime response, bank robbery de-escalation, escort, investigation, surveillance, disaster relief, recovery, security, negotiation, supernatural containment, or protection. A client may request a specific specialist, but the player can negotiate, refuse, work alone, assemble a party, or propose another solution. Contract success is not limited to defeating an opponent; safe civilians, preserved evidence, de-escalation, lawful handoff, recovered property, accurate information, and minimized collateral damage may matter more. Partial success and failure should change payment, client trust, public reputation, legal attention, faction standing, relationships, future contracts, and local conditions without ending the route. Maintain a record of accepted, active, paused, delayed, completed, failed, abandoned, and alternate-resolution contracts. Do not force a contract on the player or assume they accepted terms.
oblivions-crucible-audio-atmosphere:
Category: music and atmosphere

Name: The Crucible Audio Atmosphere

The Crucible always carries a Spooked emotional atmosphere. Whenever the player enters or remains inside the Crucible, treat the scene as eerie, unsettling, supernatural-adjacent, and watched even when nothing openly dangerous is happening. Use the Oblivion track as the location's default theme. Combat, pursuit, death, or another stronger explicit cue may temporarily override it, but the Crucible's unsettling atmosphere returns when that cue ends.
near-death-saving-throw-limit:
Category: combat and survival mechanics

Name: Near-Death Saving Throw Limit

A character may attempt at most three ordinary near-death saving throws during one continuous encounter or combat. Near-death means the character reaches a lethal threshold but remains alive and requires immediate stabilization. Dying is a separate terminal state, not an additional ordinary saving-throw loop: once the character is actually dying or declared dead, resolve one immediate intervention, then move to hospitalization or the appropriate death consequence. Do not alternate repeatedly between dying, recovering, near-death, and dying again in the same encounter. After the third near-death save, the next lethal threshold becomes a critical medical crisis resolved through immediate rescue, stabilization, an explicitly applicable healing or regeneration ability, a rare item, meaningful sacrifice, capture, hospitalization, or permanent death only when justified. Do not reset the count because the character changes rooms. A successful save leaves the character critically vulnerable and does not restore full health. Exceptional abilities may alter an outcome only when their authored requirements, resources, cooldowns, limits, and costs are satisfied. If the player dies, show one on-screen medical or supernatural intervention and then have them awaken after stabilization in an appropriate existing hospital, clinic, or specialized emergency ward.
contract-board-scams-and-escort-missions:
Category: faction and quest generation mechanics

Name: Contract Board Scams and Escort Missions

Hero for Hire and Nightshade Exchange are globally available job services when the character's role, location, legal status, reputation, and circumstances allow access. Hero for Hire handles minor rescues, escorts, security, apprehensions, disputes, and low-risk investigations. Misfit Hero Agency handles unconventional cases; Tokyo Curse Squad handles occult work; Nightshade handles criminal work; Obsidian Crown offers rare dangerous contracts; Blacklisted work is government-supervised. Every listing states objective, location, terms, payment, risks, legality, civilian danger, uncertainty, and failure conditions. Approximately 5–10% may contain scams or hidden complications, varying by reputation, verification, broker quality, urgency, and risk. Once explicitly accepted, immediately create the quest using final negotiated terms; no second confirmation is needed.
