Romantic rivals may become friendly-competing, tense, respectful, resentful, teasing, distanced, or direct. Existing committed, partnered, exclusive, or open relationships follow their established boundaries; do not assume exclusivity or non-exclusivity, and betrayal exists only relative to agreed boundaries. NPC romantic initiative is meaningful, not constant; silence, hesitation, missed opportunities, and uncertainty are valid, and attempts can fail, be interrupted, be misread, or never happen. NPC romances continue without the player and may start, deepen, drift apart, break up, reconcile, establish boundaries, or change structure only through plausible interaction, motive, time, and opportunity. Consequences may touch banter, combat synergy, schedules, invitations, friendship, rivalry, group dynamics, rumors, Pulse, mood, and quests; only those who plausibly know react. NPCs are allowed to want people and to be rejected, hesitate, make mistakes, move on, fall for someone else, or never act.
looking-for-group:
Category: party formation and hideout systems

Name: Looking for Group

LFG is an optional service for fast repeatable combat-and-loot runs. Its procedural rules apply only when the player explicitly uses Find Hideout Group to generate a new temporary Hideout. They do not apply to authored Hideouts created by the player, authored Hideouts selected directly, story Hideouts, or quest-targeted authored locations. Procedural LFG immediately forms five, uses no queue, does not block on level mismatch, runs three combat sections, awards miniboss gacha loot, and extracts quickly.

Authored Hideouts remain handcrafted adventures with their own inner areas, routes, exploration, puzzles, investigation, encounters, bosses, loot, consequences, party structure, and completion conditions. Never flatten an authored Hideout into the procedural LFG loop or impose LFG's five-person, three-section, miniboss-only, gacha, or extraction rules on it. Suppress unrelated systems only inside the LFG app.
miniboss-and-boss-generation:
Category: encounter design and boss systems

Name: Miniboss and Boss Generation

Minibosses and bosses must feel mechanically and narratively distinct from ordinary enemies; never create them as ordinary enemies with inflated health. Use unique tactics, recognizable abilities, battlefield control, phases or behavior shifts, weaknesses, resistances, environmental interaction, visual identity, and meaningful rewards. Scale from the Hideout or location level band, not directly from the player: ordinary enemies occupy lower or middle levels, strong enemies the middle or upper levels, elites the upper portion, minibosses near the upper limit or slightly above, and bosses at or moderately above the upper limit. Do not dramatically exceed the band or weaken a boss because the player is underleveled.

Minibosses are major internal obstacles. Give them 2–4 notable abilities or tactics, an exploitable weakness or limitation, stronger coordination or defenses, one signature mechanic, and stronger loot than ordinary encounters. Bosses define the Hideout or objective and should make the player do something differently: reposition, interrupt, exploit openings, manage adds, protect objectives, destroy equipment, avoid hazards, change damage type, separate, coordinate powers, or choose defense versus damage. Give bosses 3–6 meaningful abilities, one readable signature attack, a defensive or control tool, and a weakness or counter. Do not give every boss teleportation, regeneration, immunity, instant kills, endless summons, or giant area attacks. Dangerous attacks need readable telegraphs.

Boss weaknesses may involve damage type, range, mobility, setup time, exposed points, emotional instability, equipment reliance, terrain, cooldown windows, power drawbacks, summoned objects, or limited control during a strong technique. Discover them through observation, prior encounters, investigation, NPC information, environmental clues, or experimentation. Personality determines aggression, risk, targets, retreat, allies, tactics, mercy, and desperation. Generated bosses require an identity or role, level, power source, combat role, signature mechanic, abilities, weakness, motivation, Hideout relationship, reason for being present, and reward eligibility. Prefer a plausible named NPC, but never convert an unrelated authored NPC merely to fill a boss slot.

Named bosses are persistent characters; preserve defeat, capture, death, recruitment, and removal. Repeatable Hideouts use successors, replacement commanders, monsters, supported constructs or clones, evolved infestations, generic elite commanders, or new Parasite hosts. ALTERED resets may create different bosses reflecting new occupation or contamination. Every miniboss, elite objective, boss, and boss-equivalent triggers a separate gacha roll after defeat. Minibosses may grant XP, Yen, Rare-or-better chances, materials, keys, shortcuts, clues, quest progress, or supported special-drop eligibility. Bosses grant substantial XP, Yen, equipment, improved rarity odds, completion rewards, and relevant reputation or faction consequences. First-clear bosses may grant improved Rare-or-better odds, a quest reward, supported Cursed Item or Parasite eligibility, a contact, location unlock, or stronger reputation consequences, but never automatically grant a unique item. Special drops require lore-supported checks; discovery never implies ownership, equipping, bonding, infection, or activation.

Adapt party difficulty through enemies, attack angles, objectives, control, target pressure, and coordination—not boss HP or player-level scaling. Keep combat dialogue brief. Longer monologues belong before combat, at earned phase transitions, during negotiation or surrender, or after defeat; players may interrupt and act. Maintain the Knowledge Firewall.
procedural-lfg-hideout-generation:
Category: temporary LFG contracts

Name: Procedural LFG Hideout Generation

This guidance applies only to newly generated procedural LFG Hideouts. It does not govern authored Hideouts created by the player, authored Hideouts selected directly, story Hideouts, or quest-targeted authored locations. Routine procedural LFG generates a new temporary Hideout with exactly three combat sections, uses a five-person party, does not require level-matched matchmaking, and uses party average only to calibrate pressure, miniboss strength, and loot quality.

Section 1 is escalating combat. Section 2 is harder combat. Section 3 is the mandatory miniboss finale. Store all three sections before travel. After the miniboss, perform a guaranteed concrete Miniboss Gacha Loot Roll, unlock extraction, and award XP, Yen, and completion rewards. Standard procedural LFG has no boss requirement.

Authored Hideouts must preserve their own complete handcrafted structure: multiple named inner areas, connected routes, exploration, environmental storytelling, puzzles or investigation, varied encounters, optional rooms, authored minibosses or bosses, location-specific loot, consequences, and their own completion rules. Never apply the three-section procedural LFG template to an authored Hideout.
lfg-hideout-matchmaking-and-travel:
Category: LFG travel and temporary parties

Name: LFG Hideout Matchmaking and Travel Flow

These rules apply only to newly generated procedural LFG Hideouts. They do not apply to authored Hideouts created by the player, authored Hideouts selected directly, story Hideouts, or quest-targeted authored locations. When the player opens LFG, show only Find Hideout Group. Suppress starter kits, gacha menus, armories, shops, inventory, character rewards, tutorials, and unrelated systems. Selecting Find Hideout Group immediately forms exactly 5 participating characters including the player: preserve current participants and fill open slots with available willing NPCs or temporary LFG characters. Never remove members, wait in a queue, or exceed five.

Procedural LFG is a fast combat loop and does not block matchmaking over level mismatch. Finalize the five-person party and use its average level only to calibrate pressure, miniboss strength, and loot quality. Generate and store a new temporary procedural Hideout before travel. Immediately create and accept its quest. Guide Me There starts normal travel and never teleports. Use exactly three procedural sections: escalating combat, harder combat, mandatory miniboss. After miniboss resolution, roll concrete Miniboss Gacha Loot, unlock extraction, award XP/Yen/completion rewards, complete the quest, and close the instance. Standard procedural LFG requires no boss.

Authored Hideouts use their own authored rules, party structure, areas, routes, encounters, bosses, loot, extraction, and completion conditions. Do not flatten, replace, or reinterpret their inner areas as the procedural three-section LFG loop.
lfg-hideout-armory:
Category: pre-run equipment access

Name: LFG Hideout Armory

The quick gacha armory is available during any explicitly initiated LFG or compatible run preparation, regardless of story start. It presents a randomized but validated selection of real existing equippable items: Armor-category protection, Weapon-category melee, Weapon-category ranged gear, compatible ammunition, Energy Drinks, Protein Bars, and Medica Kits. Use only item records whose category and equipment slot match settings/items.json. Firearms use ranged; Shotgun, Compact Bow, and Compact Crossbow use two-hand; bows require Arrows; crossbows require Bolts; melee uses main-hand, off-hand, or two-hand; armor must use an armor slot such as body. Reject and reroll any item that cannot equip before displaying it. The player chooses what to take and nothing silently replaces existing equipment. Functional temporary Parasites and Cursed Items may appear only if they are real valid equippable Tool items with concrete effects, limits, risks, and confirmation. Items may be run-scoped and removed when the run ends unless explicitly promoted. This is a quick optional gacha preparation system, not exclusive to any story start.
lfg-hideout-armory-and-roguelike-draft:
Category: quick gacha preparation

Name: LFG Armory and Roguelike Draft

During any explicitly initiated LFG or compatible run preparation, offer a quick gacha draft from real existing item records. Each roll may present validated Armor-category protection, Weapon-category melee, Weapon-category ranged gear, compatible ammunition, Energy Drinks, Protein Bars, and Medica Kits. Use valid slots from settings/items.json: armor slots for armor; main-hand/off-hand/two-hand for melee; ranged or two-hand for ranged weapons; ammunition for compatible ammunition. Standard Ammunition supports firearms and Shotgun, Arrows support Compact Bow, and Bolts support Compact Crossbow. Reject and reroll any item that cannot actually equip before it is shown. Show item name, category, slot, effect, quantity, and whether it is permanent, loaned, or run-scoped. The player chooses rewards; never auto-equip, silently replace existing gear, or grant invented items. Temporary Parasites and Cursed Items are optional and must be valid equippable Tool records with concrete effects, costs, risks, and duration. This system is available regardless of story start.
procedural-lfg-temporary-parasites-and-c:
Category: temporary roguelike item mechanics

Name: Procedural LFG Temporary Parasites and Cursed Items

Temporary LFG starter gear must be validated against the actual item schema and slot rules before it is shown or granted. Generate only equippable items with a valid existing category and valid slot. Firearms must be existing Weapon-category ranged items: Service Pistol, Assault Rifle, Submachine Gun, Shotgun, Compact Bow, or Compact Crossbow. Service Pistol, Assault Rifle, and Submachine Gun use Standard Ammunition; Shotgun uses Standard Ammunition in the two-hand slot; Compact Bow uses Arrows in the two-hand and ammunition slots; Compact Crossbow uses Bolts in the two-hand and ammunition slots. Melee weapons must be existing Weapon-category items with a valid main-hand, off-hand, or two-hand slot, such as Training Bat or Utility Knife. Never generate armor, weapons, or attachments with invented slots, categories, level requirements, or unsupported fields.

Temporary Parasites and Cursed Items must also be represented as valid equippable Tool-category items using the cursed-item slot or another existing valid slot. Generate them as run-scoped effects only after slot/category validation, with concrete observable effects, activation, limits, costs, risks, duration, and removal. A vial or prop without an equippable effect is invalid. Show the exact item, slot, category, and equip confirmation before travel. If a generated item fails validation, discard it and generate a replacement from the valid starter pool rather than giving the player unusable gear.

Temporary items are unique to the procedural run and discarded at extraction, abandonment, interruption, or death unless explicitly promoted. Preserve the player's prior equipment and never silently replace it.
authored-hideout-structure:
Category: handcrafted hideout encounters and exploration

Name: Authored Hideout Structure

This applies only to authored Hideouts created by the player, selected directly, or targeted by a quest. Preserve every named inner area, connected route, description, and assigned art. Before entry, pre-generate and reserve the complete authored structure, including exploration routes, optional branches, hazards, objectives, concrete loot locations, a mandatory miniboss with exact identity and area, and a mandatory boss with exact identity and area whenever the Hideout's rules specify one. The miniboss and boss must actually spawn at their reserved areas; ordinary encounters cannot substitute for them. Run varied authored play across areas: entry/orientation, exploration, standard encounters, hazards/traversal, investigation, secrets, recovery/decisions, miniboss, further exploration, boss or authored conclusion, and extraction. Preserve each Hideout's own party, level, loot, extraction, and completion rules. Never flatten authored Hideouts into LFG's three-section loop or omit their miniboss/boss.
fast-hideout-pacing:
Category: authored hideout pacing

Name: Fast Hideout Pacing

All authored Hideouts must be fast-paced. Use exactly one area per Hideout. The single area contains the entire run: Entry, brief Exploration, Encounters, Hazards/Objectives, Optional Branches, Exploration Loot, Recovery/Decision, mandatory Miniboss, Further Exploration, mandatory Boss or Authored Conclusion, and Extraction. Resolve these beats in sequence without requiring the player to walk through extra rooms, search for hatches, inspect repeated doors, or perform filler traversal. Present the next meaningful beat directly after the previous beat. Optional branches are brief choices resolved within the same area and never required for progression. The miniboss and boss must spawn in this one area when the Hideout rules require them. A valid run should feel like a compact mission, not a maze.
turned-hunger-eyes:
Category: turned physiology and concealment

Name: Turned Hunger Eyes

Turned biology is publicly understood in this world: people generally know that Turned require human blood or human flesh to remain healthy and stable, and that ordinary food is rejected. Eating ordinary food causes the Turned to vomit it back up rather than digesting it. A well-fed Turned has completely normal human-looking eyes. Severe hunger changes them: the whites become completely black and the irises vivid blood-red. Hunger Eyes may appear suddenly when severely hungry, smelling blood while hungry, beginning to feed, or losing control to predatory instinct. They are a recognizable sign of a hungry Turned, so Turned may hide their eyes while starving. The eyes return to normal once hunger is sufficiently satisfied and control is restored. Do not reveal Hunger Eyes when the Turned is well-fed unless another established effect applies.
turned-evolution-and-scaling:
Name: Turned Evolution and Scaling

Turned characters scale through ordinary progression plus authored biological evolution, not automatic attribute bonuses from Turned Origin.

Turned are not vampires. They retain ordinary human teeth and a human-looking everyday appearance. Human blood and human flesh restore a Turned's health and support healing; healing speed depends on injury, amount consumed, freshness, Hunger, and player-defined limits. Turned shed blood tears when crying. Coffee, tea, and water are safe to drink but do not satisfy Hunger or replace blood or flesh; ordinary solid food remains rejected. Do not add fangs, undead traits, sunlight weakness, or other vampire conventions unless the player separately defines them. Turned Origin grants no attributes or other mechanics. The Turned power style provides feeding biology, Hunger, concealment, predatory manifestation, healing rules, blood tears, and authored Turned abilities. Leveling improves the character normally; it does not automatically increase healing, damage, regeneration, or physical attributes without an authored grant. Turned can evolve through deliberate milestones and player-chosen biological adaptations, similar to a parasite-like branching arc: controlled adaptation, witnessed breakthroughs, and costly biological choices. Each evolution should be recorded as a trait or ability with explicit benefits, limits, costs, recovery, vulnerabilities, and visible changes. Do not grant every adaptation at once or assume a form, morality, victim, loss of control, or immunity. Evolution must not erase blood or flesh requirements, food rejection, Hunger Eyes, exposure risk, or agency. Parasite-like scaling means branching tradeoffs, not automatic level-based mutation. NPCs must not reveal hidden origin, feeding history, anatomy, adaptations, or vulnerabilities without justified in-world knowledge.
dynamic-ability-damage-system-2:
Continued from dynamic-ability-damage-system (1).

Use cooldowns only for unusually powerful, broad, defensive, transformative, multi-target, or otherwise action-warping abilities, or when a specific authored drawback requires one. Show meaningful costs before use when practical. Never replace an unstated player decision with an automatic ability choice or outcome.

Stat block guidance: Attack: type, damage, damageType when established, energyCost, powerStrain, range, effect, secondaryEffect, cooldown only when warranted; basic attacks should explicitly say No Cooldown when appropriate. Defense: type, shield, energyCost, powerStrain, duration, coverage, cooldown only for unusually strong or broad defenses. Healing: type, healing, energyCost, powerStrain, range, targetLimit, restrictions, cooldown only when warranted. Buff: type, targetCapability, magnitude, energyCost, powerStrain, duration, condition, drawback, cooldown only when warranted. Debuff: type, targetCapabilityImpaired, magnitude, energyCost, powerStrain, duration, condition, counterplay, cooldown only when warranted. Other: type, effect, energyCost, powerStrain, range or area, duration when relevant, cooldown only when warranted, drawback when warranted.

Progression: Repeated meaningful use, training, experimentation, or creative development may improve an ability through higher damage, stronger shielding or healing, lower Energy cost, reduced Power Strain, added secondary effects, broader application, or an evolved version. Improvements must remain proportional to demonstrated development and may add new restrictions. Preserve the original ability's identity and player-authored intent.
dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork-2:
Continued from dynamic-ability-learning-and-teamwork (1).

Training-room attempts, field use, rescue applications, controlled experimentation, and improvised combat combinations can qualify. Merely discussing, imagining, naming, describing, agreeing to try later, or planning a combination without attempting it does not qualify. The first successful test may create a basic ability; repeated use or deliberate development can improve or evolve it. Apply the dynamic ability damage rules for type, damage or effect, Energy cost, Power Strain, cooldown, range, duration, drawbacks, and progression.
miniboss-and-boss-generation-2:
Continued from miniboss-and-boss-generation (1).

Respect lethal or nonlethal intent and allow defeat, unconsciousness, surrender, capture, escape, retreat, negotiation, or objective completion without killing. A miniboss tests the build; a boss tests understanding.
npc-initiated-romance-and-emotional-agen:
Continued from npc-initiated-romance-and-emotional-agency (1).

Romance is characters making choices, not a meter waiting for the player.
social-phone-and-friend-groups-2:
Continued from social-phone-and-friend-groups (1).

Offer concise reply choices that preserve the player's agency and do not invent the player's thoughts, feelings, dialogue, attraction, or consent. Track unanswered messages, promises, social memories, group membership, and availability. Friend groups are fluid study circles, training teams, club circles, party groups, rival cliques, roommate groups, and alliances. Groups invite, exclude, gossip, reconcile, compete, split, and reform without requiring the player's presence. Parties may occur in apartments, dorm lounges, cafés, restaurants, parks, arcades, rooftops, or hidden venues. Parties can improve relationships, create jealousy or rumors, expose secrets, trigger romance or rivalry, produce invitations, or create curfew or house-rule risk where such rules apply. Preserve individual agency: attendance is never guaranteed and romance remains gradual, mutual, consent-based, and distinct from friendship.
fit-and-fashion-expansion: Fashion is optional inventory-driven spending. Clothing and accessories use body, head, feet, hands, ear, or accessory slots. The accessory slot quantity is five, while ear slots remain separate. Rings are cosmetic and may be worn in any number as a visual choice; they do not consume slots unless an authored ring has a mechanical effect. Piercings are cosmetic body-modification services or appearance records, including ear, nose, eyebrow, lip, and other player-chosen placements, with safe professional care and aftercare. Tattoos are cosmetic appearance records or studio services with player-defined designs, placement, scale, color, visibility, and cultural meaning. Neither piercings nor tattoos grant automatic bonuses, imply personality or morality, or override consent. Nail and hair purchases update appearance rather than stack as equipment. Designer pieces, premium salons, spas, piercers, tattoo studios, and onsen packages are optional luxury sinks with no required combat advantage. They may support authored social scenes, invitations, photos, discounts, or venue access. Require yen, plausible time, professional access, aftercare, and player choice. Never infer personality, gender, sexuality, class, morality, or consent from appearance.
item-upgrading-and-turned-materials: Gear can be upgraded at Gearshift Support, with lawful specialist alternatives at Gearshift Support Shop and Redline Arms and Armor. Characters may also upgrade their own weapons, armor, cursed items, and utility gear at an appropriate workshop bench, home work area, or other authored facility. Self-upgrades require yen, materials, time, tools, and a suitable approach. Intelligence determines the maximum self-upgrade tier and the quality of the result: higher Intelligence permits higher tiers, reduces material waste and failure risk, and improves reliability; lower Intelligence may still succeed at simpler tiers but makes advanced work riskier. Upgrades may improve damage, durability, reliability, utility, or special properties; cosmetics are never required for combat. Materials include Stable Flesh from voluntary cooperative Turned donors, Predatory Tissue from hostile Turned combat drops, and Manifestation Core as a rare high-grade material from exceptional Turned sources. Voluntary harvesting requires informed consent, trust, fair compensation or favors, medical safety, and clear boundaries. Combat materials may be unstable, contaminated, ethically troubling, or unpredictable. Vermine may offer illicit upgrades using unstable material, with serious risks and consequences. Never force harvesting, feeding, transformation, or morality onto a player or NPC.
turned-factions-and-conflict: Turned NPCs are not morally uniform. Some are friendly or cooperative civilians, medics, workers, artists, donors, or mutual-aid organizers. Others are neutral, concealed, traumatized, independent, feral, or actively dangerous. Feral Turned may attack from hunger, fear, isolation, or loss of control, but do not make every hungry Turned feral automatically. Vermine is a morally divided Turned faction containing mutual-aid cells, ideological organizers, and terrorists who attack humans, corporations, public infrastructure, or symbolic targets. A Vermine affiliation does not erase individual motives or permit automatic villainization of every Turned person. The Blacklisted Redemption Program actively hunts, captures, evaluates, or redeploys suspected Turned targets under its own legal and operational justification. This conflict should create investigation, negotiation, rescue, pursuit, betrayal, and combat possibilities. Do not force a faction choice, reveal concealed Turned identities without evidence, or treat biological requirements as proof of guilt.
vehicles-and-ownership: Characters may purchase and own cars or motorcycles through lawful dealerships such as Velvet Apex Motors. Ownership requires payment or approved financing, identity and licensing checks, registration, insurance, and a plausible parking or storage arrangement. Multiple vehicles are allowed when the character can afford and maintain them. Vehicles provide travel convenience, lifestyle scenes, storage, commuting options, social status, and authored customization, but do not grant automatic combat bonuses or bypass travel, legal access, traffic, fuel or charging, maintenance, parking, or weather. Cars and motorcycles can be customized cosmetically or mechanically through authored services. Motorcycles require appropriate licensing and safety gear. Stolen vehicles, reckless driving, illegal modifications, and evading registration create consequences.
